name: What is FIRPTA and how does it affect international home buyers?

mainEntity.name: What is FIRPTA and how does it affect international home buyers?

acceptedAnswer.text: FIRPTA (Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act) is a U.S. tax law that imposes income tax on foreign persons selling U.S. real property interests. When an international owner sells property, a portion of the sale price (currently 15%) is typically withheld by the buyer and remitted to the IRS. This is not an additional tax but a withholding mechanism to ensure capital gains tax is paid. Understanding FIRPTA is part of the preparation needed for a future sale.
acceptedAnswer.description: FIRPTA is a U.S. tax law requiring buyers to withhold a portion of the sale price when an international owner sells U.S. real estate.
